summary: RE-TEST of the CRITICAL lockout-bypass bug from iteration_61.json (T09 Evidence Locker PinGate). The 4-layer defense-in-depth fix (submittingRef serialization, fresh storage re-read of getLockoutRemainingMs() in submit(), onChangeText ignoring input while locked, pointerEvents='none' on the Pressable) IS EFFECTIVE and genuinely closes the bug. Tested the EXACT same bypass technique that succeeded in iteration_61 (plain, non-forced Playwright click during an actively-counting-down lockout) and it now correctly FAILS to even reach the button (Playwright's own actionability check times out because pointer-events:none is now actually applied on the DOM, not just aria-disabled). Also tried a more aggressive forced fill() + forced click() (bypassing Playwright's actionability checks entirely) specifically to simulate a malicious/automated bypass attempt -- the PIN input value remained empty (onChangeText correctly ignored the forced input) and the forced click on the button still did not call onUnlock() (submit()'s fresh storage re-check caught it). Locker correctly stayed on the PIN gate / locked in all bypass attempts. After waiting out the full 30s lockout window, the Unlock button re-enabled, countdown text disappeared, and the correct PIN then unlocked normally. A wrong-PIN attempt submitted mid-lockout (via forced fill/click) did not reset/extend the lockout (29s observed immediately after, consistent with natural 1s tick, not a reset to 30s) -- confirmed by code: submit() returns early on freshLockoutMs>0 before ever calling verifyPin(), so wrong attempts during lockout can never increment PIN_ATTEMPTS_KEY or rewrite PIN_LOCKOUT_KEY. Quick regressions also pass: first-visit Set PIN -> Confirm PIN -> unlock works; correct PIN re-entry (no prior lockout) unlocks immediately.
critical_code_review_comments: Fix verified sound: the key change vs. iteration_61 is that submit() now re-reads getLockoutRemainingMs() directly from storage at the TOP of every call (not trusting the lockoutMs closure), which is the correct authoritative security boundary -- even if UI-level guards (disabled/pointerEvents/onChangeText) were somehow bypassed, this storage-level recheck independently blocks the unlock.

pointerEvents='none' combined with disabled={locked} now genuinely blocks pointer-events at the DOM level on web (previously only aria-disabled was set, which Playwright/real taps could click through) -- this closes the specific DOM-level gap noted in iteration_61.
No regressions observed in PIN creation, correct unlock, lockout trigger/countdown, or lockout non-extension by mid-lockout wrong attempts.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The T09 lockout-bypass bug is CLOSED and verified via: (1) plain non-forced click during active, visibly-ticking-down lockout (30s->27s observed) -- blocked, Playwright itself times out trying to click because pointer-events:none now applies; (2) forced fill()+forced click() bypass attempt -- input stayed empty, click fired onPress but submit()'s storage-level recheck rejected it, locker stayed locked; (3) after full 30s expiry, correct PIN unlocked normally; (4) wrong PIN attempted mid-lockout did not reset/extend the 30s window. Note for future testers: each new browser_automation tool call in this environment starts a FRESH browser context (no persisted cookies/localStorage across separate tool invocations) -- the full consent->login->set-PIN->lockout->bypass->expiry flow must be scripted as ONE single script call, not split across multiple calls, or you'll hit spurious redirects back to /consent or /login.
